description: The line plot compares the performance of six different methods across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with labeled major ticks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to above 85, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 5 units. Six solid lines with distinct colors and markers represent the different methods, all of which display a steady upward trend across the four data points plotted along the x-axis. The "Base" method is depicted by a black line with circular markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 63% at the first data point and rising to roughly 77% at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, increasing from about 64% to 79%. The "IKE" method, represented by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, rises from approximately 66% to 81%. The "MEND" method uses a brown line with diamond markers, starting at roughly 67% and ending at approximately 84%. The "MEMIT" method is illustrated by a purple line with pentagonal markers, beginning at about 68% and increasing to roughly 83%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers, starting at the highest initial value of approximately 74% and climbing to end at roughly 86%.
